title: Consulting
description: Intellica consulting: AI readiness reviews, architecture for AI-assisted delivery, AI and agent engineering, governance, post-quantum readiness and AI value proof. Check where you stand with three free self-assessments.

hero.title: AI that works in your organisation, and evidence that it does.
hero.lead: Intellica helps engineering, risk and finance leaders adopt AI with their eyes open: find where you really stand, fix the foundations that decide whether AI helps or hurts, and leave with results your own team can check.

why.title: The evidence says: AI amplifies what is already there
why.lead: Four findings that shape how we work. None of them says AI does not work. All of them say the result depends on the foundations, and on measuring instead of assuming.

cards.title: AI magnifies your existing practice
cards.text: The 2025 DORA report on AI-assisted software development concludes that AI's primary role is that of an amplifier: strong practices get stronger, and weak ones get exposed.

cards.title: Feeling faster is not being faster
cards.text: In a randomised trial of 16 experienced open-source developers on 246 real tasks, using AI tools made them 19% slower. They expected a 24% speed-up and still believed they had been about 20% faster afterwards. The authors stress that this is early-2025 tools in one setting.

cards.title: Context files are not free
cards.text: An ETH Zurich study reported in March 2026 found that machine-generated agent context files lowered coding-agent success by about 3% while raising inference cost by over 20%. Developer-written files helped only slightly (about 4%). What you write, and how short you keep it, matters.

cards.title: The rules are moving; the expectation is not
cards.text: The EU's 2026 AI omnibus moved the high-risk obligations of the AI Act to 2 December 2027 (stand-alone systems) and 2 August 2028 (AI inside regulated products). The dates slipped. The expectation that you can show what AI you run and how you control it did not.

how.title: Four habits that run through every engagement

items.p: Every deliverable says how to verify it yourself. If we cannot say how, we do not claim it.
We set the baseline first. Without one, a result is an anecdote.
We write things down, teach the method and hand over the tools. You should need us less each month.
Markdown, open standards and tests that run in your pipeline. Nothing locks you in.

steps.p: We agree the question, the evidence we will produce and the end date, in writing.
We work alongside your team on your real system, with a short written update each week.
You receive the documents, tests and tools, and how to re-run them.

assess.title: Check where you stand in five minutes
assess.lead: Three short assessments. Each answer describes something observable, so you can pick what is true today instead of what you hope is true. Scores are worked out in your browser: nothing is sent or stored anywhere else unless you choose to share it.
assess.note: In Cisco's first AI Readiness Index (2023), 14% of 8,161 organisations surveyed were fully ready across six pillars: strategy, infrastructure, data, talent, governance and culture. Self-assessments tend to run optimistic, so when two answers seem to fit, choose the lower one.
assess.caveat: A self-assessment shows you where to look. An evidence-based review confirms what you find.
